elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Revised 21.1: "each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed the greater of fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000" — the cap runs to both Parties symmetrically, and no residual unlimited-Customer-liability language survives.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: 21.1 as rendered uses the exact preferred construction: "the greater of fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000" (basis is 'paid or payable', lookback anchored to the claim, floor stated in USD 1,000,000). Note the lowercase 'fees' no longer invokes defined "Fees" (§1.5), which is at worst neutral/broadening.

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained 21.2: "neither Party is liable for indirect, incidental, special, exemplary, punitive, or consequential damages, or for lost profits, revenues, or goodwill" — mutual by its terms and untouched by the redline.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.1 now opens "Except for Excluded Claims" (deleting the original "without exception"), and 21.3 defines Excluded Claims to include "a Party's breach of confidentiality... obligations", so confidentiality breach sits outside the cap.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims include "breach of confidentiality, data-protection, or security obligations", and 21.1's new "Except for Excluded Claims" opener carries them outside the monetary cap.
21.3 lists "its indemnification obligations" within Excluded Claims; the reinstated exception in 21.1 removes them from the cap (no super-cap or residual override remains).
21.3: "gross negligence, wilful misconduct, or fraud" are Excluded Claims, excepted from the 21.1 cap.
21.3 includes "wilful misconduct" in Excluded Claims; 21.1 is now expressly subject to that exception.
21.3 includes "fraud" in Excluded Claims, which 21.1 now excepts from the aggregate cap.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3: "infringement or misappropriation of the other Party's intellectual property" is an Excluded Claim, outside the revised 21.1 cap.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Revised 21.3 still reads "Customer's obligation to pay undisputed amounts due for conforming Services is not damages and is not limited by this Section." Broadening "Fees" to "amounts due" helps, but the retained "undisputed" and "for conforming Services" qualifiers confine the carve-out to a subset of Customer's payment obligations rather than payment obligations as a whole; the deterministic payment-carve-out check also returns false.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: 21.1: "each Party's aggregate liability shall not exceed..." — expressly bilateral.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: 21.1 sets the cap by reference to "fees paid or payable in the twelve months preceding the claim" (with a USD 1,000,000 floor), replacing the one-month basis.
"Except for Excluded Claims" in 21.1 plus 21.3's inclusion of "its indemnification obligations" places indemnities outside the cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: 21.3 Excluded Claims include breach of confidentiality obligations, now excepted from the 21.1 cap.
21.3 Excluded Claims include gross negligence; 21.1 excepts Excluded Claims.
21.3 Excluded Claims include wilful misconduct; 21.1 excepts Excluded Claims.

reasons: Deviation call is correct: original 21.1 capped both Parties at one month of defined "Fees" "without exception", which is below the six-month walk-away floor and cancelled the Excluded Claims regime in 21.2-21.3, pulling indemnities, confidentiality, data protection/security, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and IP infringement inside a one-month cap.

Position-complete at the fallback level: all six fallback elements are met in operative language (mutual cap, 12-months'-fees basis, and uncapped indemnification, confidentiality, gross negligence and wilful misconduct).

Preferred level is one element short. To close it, amend 21.3 to read along the lines of "Customer's obligation to pay amounts due under this Agreement is not damages and is not limited by this Section" — the retained "undisputed" and "for conforming Services" qualifiers mean only a subset of Customer's payment obligations is carved out, so the element is not literally satisfied. Note the trade-off: those qualifiers are Customer-favourable, so leaving them and resting at the fallback is a defensible choice that should be stated in the comment rather than claiming the preferred position.

Minimality holds: the only edits are (i) deleting "without exception" and inserting "Except for Excluded Claims" in 21.1, (ii) replacing the one-month "Fees actually paid" basis with the preferred greater-of formula, and (iii) the narrow "Fees" to "amounts due" swap in 21.3 — each maps to a checklist element. Favourable retained language (21.2 direct-damages sentence, undisputed/conforming qualifiers, mutual exclusion) is preserved and nothing extraneous (survival tails, procedures, new damages categories) is added.

Intent preserved: 21.2 and 21.3 remain coherent, the 21.1 reference to "Excluded Claims" resolves to the 21.3 definition, and no cross-reference is left dangling. Drafting nit only: 21.1 now uses lowercase "fees" rather than defined "Fees" and omits "paid or payable by Customer under this Agreement"; consider restoring that phrase for precision, since defined "Fees" (§1.5) excludes taxes, expenses and implementation charges.

Margin comment slightly overstates the outcome — it should not imply the payment carve-out now covers Customer payment obligations generally; recast it as reaching the fallback with the payment carve-out left qualified in our favour.
